804.author: HugoXK
804.body:
Fixes #794

## What changed

`apps/desktop/src/views/Composer.tsx` (the `/` palette's Enter at line 837, the send at line 844), `Sidebar.tsx:165` (rename field) and `PromptDialog.tsx:110` (dialog accept) each read `event.key === "Enter"` and acted on it. While an IME candidate is open that Enter belongs to the IME: the composer sent the draft with the pinyin still in it (`蛋白` instead of the `蛋白质` still being chosen), the palette could select a skill, and the two single-line fields could commit.

The four listeners now share one pure rule, `apps/desktop/src/app/ime-enter.ts`:

- `commitsOnEnter(event)` is false unless `key === "Enter"`;
- false while `nativeEvent.isComposing` or a top-level `isComposing` is true — React keeps the flag on the native event, a bare KeyboardEvent has it on itself;
- false for `keyCode === 229`, the form some IMEs (notably on Windows) report for the confirming Enter without setting any composition flag;
- true otherwise, so the Enter after the candidate is accepted still sends and accepts as before.

Shift+Enter stays at the call site, because it differs there: the composer still requires `!shiftKey` before it sends, while the single-line rename and dialog fields have no newline to give it to. Nothing else in the four listeners changed; no devDependency was added, and no DOM is needed because the rule is a pure function.

## Validation

Red at the parent commit `87fbbd1ad7d747822952845519ce06eb95f38430` (the tests-only commit), run again on that commit before the fix:

```
# tests 10
# pass 4
# fail 6
```

with, for the composer case, `Expected values to be strictly equal: true !== false` (`expected: false`, `actual: true`). The six failures are exactly the composition paths: composer send, palette selection, sidebar rename, dialog accept, the native-event-only shape, and keyCode 229. The four control cases (composition ended, Shift+Enter left to the caller, non-Enter keys) pass on both sides.

Green at this tip:

```
# tests 10
# pass 10
# fail 0
```

## Ran

- `cd apps/desktop && ../../node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` → 707 tests, 707 pass, 0 fail (697 on this branch's base; the new file adds 10).
- `cd apps/desktop && ../../node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` → exit 0.
- `grep -n commitsOnEnter apps/desktop/src/views/*.tsx` → `Composer.tsx:837`, `Composer.tsx:844`, `Sidebar.tsx:165`, `PromptDialog.tsx:110`; no listener keeps its own Enter predicate.

## Not run

- No browser or IME journey: the desktop composer has no page test in this repository and the composition timing is the platform's; acceptance here is the pure rule plus the existing component suite staying green.
- Root `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` and `pnpm --recursive typecheck` still fail with the 7 pre-existing module-resolution errors in `packages/execution-router` and `services/api` reported on #785 and #792; none is in `apps/desktop`.

## Labels

Could not add a `release:*` label: the token has no label permission on `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` (403). A maintainer needs to apply exactly one.

805.author: HugoXK
805.body:
Fixes #795

## What changed

`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts`: `buildJsonPreview` now applies the rule the CSV/TSV path already uses (`splitDelimited`) — strip exactly one leading `U+FEFF` and only at the start — before `JSON.parse`. A BOM is an encoding marker, not document content, so a JSON artifact written by a Windows tool previews as a table or formatted JSON instead of "not valid JSON".

## Ran

- Red, on the branch parent `0b6286ef` plus the test commit only: `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts` → `pass 44 / fail 1`; failure `not ok 22 - a JSON document saved with a UTF-8 BOM still previews as a table` with `BOM-JSON {"mode":"json-source","parsed":false}`.
- Green, on this tip: same command → `pass 45 / fail 0`.
- The test pins the three acceptance cases: a BOM record array previews as `dataset-table` (`columns ["name","value"]`, rows `[["af3","1"],["af3b","2"]]`); a BOM scalar document previews as `json-source` with `parsed: true` and the re-indented source; a `U+FEFF` inside a string survives the strip.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test` → `# tests 1777 / # pass 1772 / # fail 5`. All five are environment gaps, none in the preview code: `not ok 778` (real uvicorn research run), `not ok 959`, `not ok 961`, `not ok 1339` (PDF extraction, needs reportlab), `not ok 1516` (nested-userns Codex runner).
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck` → exit 0.
- Single-test probe: `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts --test-name-pattern "UTF-8 BOM"`.

## Not run

- L1/L2/L3 E2E layers, `services/gateway` and `packages/*` suites, real browser UI: this change only alters preview parsing, covered by the UT above.

## Impact

- JSON artifacts saved with a BOM (typical of Windows tooling) now render as a table or formatted JSON in the preview panel.
- CSV/TSV parsing, content sniffing, and `>2^53` number handling are untouched.
- No public API, schema or stored-format change.

810.author: HugoXK
810.body:
Fixes #809

## What changed

Two files, and the split matters for review: `services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` **+99/−3** is the whole production change (one linear scan in `protectBigIntegers`, the token map, and the restore calls on the three render paths), while `services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts` **+329/−0** is new tests only — no production code there. `JSON.parse` rounds every integer beyond 2^53, so a stored 64-bit id previewed with different digits than the document holds. The preview now keeps the stored literal:

- `protectBigIntegers` walks the document once, copies strings verbatim, and replaces only integer tokens that `JSON.parse` cannot represent (`!Number.isSafeInteger`) with placeholders before parsing.
- Each placeholder is minted per document: `createBigIntegerMarker()` returns a fresh random uuid prefix (U+0001 … U+0002), a counter keeps the placeholders within one document distinct, and the controls cannot appear in a JSON string without an escape, so text a user wrote can never be a placeholder.
- `restoreBigIntegers` puts the digits back through an exact token→literal map on the three render paths: table cells, `rawJson.source`, and the `json-source` view. The quoted shape written by `JSON.stringify` is restored first, so the digits come back as a JSON **number**, not as a string holding the digits; the bare shape used by table cells comes second. A safe number keeps its exact old rendering, and a string that merely looks like a big number is never touched.

No new dependency, no change to `packages/artifact-manager`, jobs, CAS or storage; the #805 BOM strip is untouched.

The earlier tip `b397911b` is superseded: it restored only the bare placeholder, so the raw and source views emitted `"sample_id": "9007199254740993"` (a string where the document holds a number) and its fixed `sd-bigint:` prefix could be forged by document text. This tip fixes both.

## Ran

- Red, on the branch parent `8708320f` plus the test commit only: `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts` → `# tests 52 / # pass 47 / # fail 5`; failures `not ok 48 - json preview keeps big integers as numbers in the raw and source views`, `49 - json preview leaves user text that spells an old placeholder untouched`, `50 - json preview round-trips a big integer document through JSON.parse`, `51 - big integer placeholders are generated per document and are not the old prefix`, `52 - json preview keeps placeholders for many big integers apart`. The original case still failed the same way (`not ok 46`, cell `9007199254740992` vs `9007199254740993`).
- Green, on this tip `7ac867dc`: same command → `# tests 52 / # pass 52 / # fail 0`.
- The new block covers, text-level and type-level:
  - record array `[{"sample_id":9007199254740993,"label":"x"}]` → `dataset-table`; the cell is `9007199254740993`, `rawJson.source` matches `"sample_id": 9007199254740993` with the digit string `9007199254740993`, and never contains `"9007199254740993"`.
  - `{"run_id":12345678901234567890}` → `json-source`, `parsed: true`, matches `"run_id": 12345678901234567890`.
  - a bare scalar `9007199254740993` → source is exactly `9007199254740993`; `[9007199254740993]` → `[\n  9007199254740993\n]`, digits taken from the text, not from a rounded parse.
  - `JSON.parse(rawJson.source)` / `JSON.parse(source)` deep-equal the stored document's `JSON.parse` (structure is not disturbed by the placeholders), alongside the digit-string assertions above.
  - document text that spells the retired `sd-bigint:` sentinel survives character for character, with and without a real big integer in the same document; a token shape the call never minted also survives.
  - `createBigIntegerMarker()` returns a different value per call, carries the U+0001 prefix, and does not start with the retired `sd-bigint:`.
  - 12 distinct big integers in one document keep their own digits (placeholders whose counters share a prefix never eat each other).
  - regression: `42` stays `"42"`, a `"9007199254740993"` string stays a string, a nested object still renders as `JSON.stringify(value, null, 2)`.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test` on this tip → `# tests 1784 / # pass 1779 / # fail 5`. All five are the known environment gaps, none in the preview code: `not ok 785` (real uvicorn research run), `not ok 966`, `968`, `1346` (PDF extraction, needs reportlab), `not ok 1523` (nested-userns Codex runner).
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck` → exit 0.
- Single file probe: `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts`.

## Not run

- L2/L3 E2E layers, `services/gateway` and `packages/*` suites, real browser UI: the change is confined to preview rendering and covered by the UT above.

## Impact

- Artifacts that store 64-bit identifiers (`sample_id`, `run_id`, timestamps in nanoseconds) now preview with the digits they hold, in the table cell, the raw JSON view and the JSON source view — and the raw/source views keep them as JSON numbers.
- Safe numbers, strings and nested values render exactly as before; CSV/TSV parsing and job shapes are untouched.
- No public API, schema or stored-format change.

814.author: ink999107
814.body:
## Problem

Evolve is the one capability that keeps running and producing results after the turn that started it ends, but the desktop app had no way to reach it: `/evolve-design` opened nothing, so a search could only be designed, confirmed and watched in the web client. A user working in the desktop app has to switch surfaces mid-task, and the run they left behind is unreachable from where they are.

## What this adds

- **Create dialog** — collects the two things a person actually knows (what should get better, which search algorithm fits) and hands that sentence to the conversation as the command the user would have typed. The agent still designs the scorecard, runs the probe and owns the checkpoints.
- **Checkpoint pace switch** — on by default. Turning it off sends `/evolve-design --no-confirm`: the agent still does the work of every step and still reports each checkpoint, labelled as automatic, but does not wait for a reply between them. Checkpoint 3's cost summary is kept, and a blocker that needs a decision (missing dataset, ambiguous goal, an approval the agent cannot give) still stops. The pace is recorded on the goal as `checkpointMode`; an absent field reads as `confirm`, which is what every existing run did.
- **Checkpoint cards** — each of the four checkpoints is drawn as a card in the transcript rather than as more prose: the step (`检查点 1/4`), the question, the few lines to read, and two answers — confirm and continue, or put "I'd like to change this step:" in the composer. A run with the pace switch off still shows the card, marked automatic, with no buttons. The card is read from the answer's own `evolve-checkpoint` fence, so it survives a reload; a client that does not draw cards falls back to the block as readable code.
- **Session shelf** — a thin row under the session header. A running search stays reachable when the panel is closed, and a session that never used evolve renders exactly as before.
- **Result panel** — follows the run's SSE stream, falls back to polling the run list, and answers in order: best score and how it moved, the candidate table, a selected candidate's diff, and why it was rejected. The inspector becomes a drawer on a narrow window.

## Tests

- `apps/desktop`: `npm run typecheck`; `npm test` — 752 pass, including new command parsing, dialog, shelf, panel, pace-switch, checkpoint-fence and checkpoint-card cases.
- `services/api` evolution suites (proposal, pre-flight, call budget, thinking control) — 51/51.
- `packages/evolve` 11/11, `packages/schema` 29/29.
- The desktop e2e suite gains `apps/desktop/e2e/evolve.spec.ts` with a mocked evolve runtime, including three checkpoint-card journeys: confirm sends the reply, an automatic card asks for nothing, and the change button fills the composer without sending. Playwright is not installed in this worktree, so it runs in CI rather than locally.

## Acceptance

The end-to-end path is the tutorial sample in `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md` (Chinese: `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`), and the UI review tracked in #798 is the other acceptance item.

Related to #798 — this PR does not close it.

814.title: feat(desktop): support program evolution in the desktop app

821.author: wyhohyw
821.body:
Fixes #812

Draft. Evolve can score a search from an NPU shell execution, and a scorecard can limit which fields a candidate is allowed to change.

## Summary
- An NPU search submits a signed `POST /shell-executions` to the Runner and waits. Success is `completed` with `device` equal to `npu`. A queued, running, failed, or non-NPU result has no numeric score, and it is not stored as 0. The local sandbox is not used as a fallback.
- The scorecard names `direction.editable`. A candidate that is not that JSON object, or that changes any other field, is refused before it is scored. A search with no direction is unchanged.

## Test plan
- [x] `services/evolve/tests/test_npu_direction.py`: 4 passed. Covers a fixed-field rejection, refusal without a direction or a runner, a non-NPU result, and one signed submit that waits from running to an NPU score.
- [ ] A real Runner with an Ascend device.

830.author: HugoXK
830.body:
Fixes #829

## Review answers — the four threads on `3b41ee80`

Three reviewers independently found the same hole in the first attempt, and the second one is worse than the first: when a table crossed the cell budget the preview returned the **pre-fix shape** — the sheared grid `#829` is about — and nothing in the payload said so. The column set was even a property of the request, since the budget was divided by the rows the client asked for: the same file came back square at `maxRows=100` and sheared at `maxRows=1000` (1000 columns × 100 rows square, 1001 columns × 100 rows sheared). Fixing one end and leaving the other is what all four threads attacked, so the branch no longer has a shape fork at all.

**Now (this tip `286255c83e9f9c44888dd54cbd2d53252e54d219`):**

- The rectangle is unconditional. The **width** is capped, never abandoned: `cap = max(header.columns, floor(MAX_PREVIEW_CELLS / file rows))`, `width = min(widest returned row, cap)`, and every row is padded or sliced to that width.
- The divisor is the **file's own row count** (`totalRows`, known while scanning), never the returned rows. `maxRows` is a client query parameter and no longer decides how the table looks: the cap is a property of the file.
- `totalRows` 0 and 1 are both defined — the divisor is `max(totalRows, 1)`, so the cap is the whole budget and no division by zero or infinity is reachable.
- **The header is a floor**: `cap` never falls below the header's column count, so no named column is ever dropped. A legitimate 200-column table is previewed whole.
- **Clipping is reported, not silent**: the payload carries `clippedCells` (0 when the table came back whole — it is not a flag that is always on), and the viewer prints it through `artifact.tableClippedCells` (en + zhCN). `#822`'s JSON path reports 0.
- **The one user-visible loss, stated plainly**: surplus cells past the cap do not enter the preview. They are not dropped from the artifact — only from this preview — and the count is shown to the reader.

Forbidden: I could also have kept the ragged fallback and added a `ragged` flag. That leaves the shear for exactly the wide tables this PR claims to fix, and makes the row shape depend on `maxRows`, so it was not taken.

### Measured, four groups (`columns` / `cells` / response bytes / `cap`)

| case | columns | cells | bytes | cap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 named columns, 2 rows | 100 | 200 | 2,338 | 50,000 |
| 200 named columns, 2 rows | 200 | 400 | 4,438 | 50,000 |
| 1001-column header, 100 rows (3 cells each) | 1001 | 100,100 | 308,264 | 1,001 |
| 101 columns, 1200 rows ragged, `maxRows=1000` | 101 | 101,000 | 674,165 | 101 |
| 101 columns, 1200 rows ragged, `maxRows=100` | 101 | 10,100 | 68,465 | 101 |
| pathological: 2-column header, 100 rows, one 200,001-cell line | 1000 | 100,000 | 304,973 | 1,000 |

Every one of those is square (`row.length === columns.length` for all rows). The 1001-column and 101-column cases exceed 100,000 cells by 0.1% on purpose: the header floor wins over the last fraction of the budget, because dropping a named column is worse than 100 extra cells.

Two limits worth stating rather than implying:

1. The cap is independent of `maxRows`; the **width** still comes from the widest *returned* row (`#829`'s rule, pinned by an existing test). A pathological line outside the `maxRows` window can therefore still change the column count — but it cannot produce the shear/square fork and it cannot amplify, because the cap does not move with `maxRows`.
2. `MAX_PREVIEW_CELLS = DEFAULT_MAX_CHARS = 100_000` — the preview's existing budget for a text source, not a new constant. One cell is a few bytes of JSON, so 100k cells lands in the same order of bytes as 100k characters (~0.3–0.8 MB here), and a table preview never spends more than the text it came from already does. 60k would cut legitimate 1001-column headers harder; 500k would multiply the response without buying any table a reader can use.

## What changed

Five files, `+258/−8` against `865102a3`:

| file | change | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| `services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` | +57/−5 | the cap, the pad/slice, `clippedCells` |
| `services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts` | +191/−0 | tests only |
| `apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx` | +6/−3 | viewer shows the clipped count |
| `apps/web/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` | +2/−0 | payload type mirror |
| `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` | +2/−0 | `artifact.tableClippedCells`, en and zhCN |

`parseDelimitedTable` returned `columns: lines[0]` next to `rows: lines.slice(1, maxRows + 1)`, so a row kept whatever width the file gave it, while the renderer prints one `<th>` per column and one `<td>` per cell (`apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx:248` and `:249`, no padding, no truncation on either side). One ragged line sheared the whole grid: an extra cell landed under no header, a short row left the tail cells empty.

The preview is now a rectangle: width `min(widest returned row, cap)`, header names first and in order, extra columns named `""`, short rows padded with `""`. `totalRows` and `truncated` are computed exactly as before, and the JSON record-array path (`recordArrayTable`) is untouched apart from reporting `clippedCells: 0`.

No new dependency, no manifest or lockfile change, no change to `packages/artifact-manager`, jobs or CAS.

## Ran

Commits, in order: `ff2046aa` (test: pad to the announced width) → `5644f0b7` (fix) → `46a83363` (test: bound the cells a wide row may add) → `3b41ee80` (fix: cell budget) → `286255c8` (test + fix: cap the width, report what left).

- Red at the first test commit `ff2046aa` (before `5644f0b7`): `# tests 60 / # pass 59 / # fail 1`, `not ok 60 - a delimited preview keeps every row as wide as the columns it advertises`; first difference `short.csv` row `["1","2"]` where the test expects `["1","2",""]`.
- Red at the second test commit `46a83363` (before `3b41ee80`): `# tests 62 / # pass 61 / # fail 1` — `the outlier row must not add blank columns: 200001 !== 3`.
- Red at the fourth test commit (before the cap landed): **`64 tests / 60 pass / 4 fail`** — all four new cases red at once, which is what the four threads were pointing at:

```
not ok - a delimited preview caps its width instead of copying one pathological line into every row
  2 !== 1000                          (the old un-padded branch)
not ok - a delimited preview keeps a header wider than the budget whole
  3 !== 1001                          (100 x 1001 = 100,100 cells crossed the budget and fell back)
not ok - a delimited preview returns the same columns whatever maxRows it is asked for
  50 !== 101                          (the maxRows=1000 case was not square)
not ok - a delimited preview returns a legitimately wide table whole
  undefined !== 0                     (clippedCells did not exist yet)
```

- Green at this tip `286255c83e9f9c44888dd54cbd2d53252e54d219`: **`64 / 64 / 0`**; `#650`'s quoted-delimiter case, `#654`'s BOM case and the "a row past `maxRows` must not add a column" case are all in that file and green.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck` → exit 0; `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web typecheck` → exit 0 (the viewer and the i18n file changed).
- Full suite `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test` → `# tests 1832 / # pass 1826 / # fail 6`, the same six environment failures as on the untouched base (`826` uvicorn, `988`, `1007`/`1009`/`1392` reportlab, `1569` Codex userns), none of them in this file.

## Not run

- No browser journey: the change is inside the API response plus one meta line in the viewer. The response shape is pinned by the API cases above; the viewer line is a string interpolation over `clippedCells`, covered by the payload tests rather than by a DOM test.

## Labels

If the token cannot apply a `release:*` label, a maintainer needs to add exactly one (the previous PR hit a 403 there).

[Bug] The remaining Enter sites act on the Enter that confirms an IME candidate

Owner: Dev-1
Written-by: Dev-1

## What changed

`#794`/`#804` gave the desktop composer, the `/` palette, the sidebar rename and the prompt dialog one pure rule, `commitsOnEnter(event)`. Six more Enter listeners were left on the bare predicate, in four shapes:

| Site | Old predicate | What the confirming Enter did |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apps/web/src/SshKeyFileField.tsx:84` | `event.key === "Enter"` | browsed the half-typed path (`["~/.ssh"]` instead of the directory being typed) |
| `apps/web/src/session/ManagementControls.tsx:67` | `event.key !== "Enter" \|\| event.nativeEvent.isComposing` | committed the rename while the pinyin was still being chosen; read only the native flag, so `keyCode 229` and a top-level `isComposing` slipped through |
| `apps/web/src/App.tsx:5052` | same half-guard as above | the same rename commit on the session header |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/RunnerResources.tsx:589` | `event.key !== "Enter"` | asked for the key-file listing a second time (2 requests for one Enter) |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/system/Timeouts.tsx:159` | `event.key !== "Enter"` | committed the timeout field without blurring first |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/ModelForm.tsx:200` | `event.key === "Enter"` | picked the highlighted model while the candidate was open (`''` → `'gpt-4o-mini'`) |

All six now call `commitsOnEnter(event)`; the predicates read exactly one rule and no site keeps its own copy. Shift handling stays at each call site where it differs (`App.tsx:5052` keeps `event.shiftKey` first, as the composer already did).

`apps/web` and `apps/desktop` each keep their own copy of the rule (`apps/web/src/ime-enter.ts:36`, `apps/desktop/src/app/ime-enter.ts:36`). They are byte-identical, and each app has the same group of rule tests. The web app cannot import from `apps/desktop`, and the rule is 12 lines, so a shared package or a `@sciencediscvery/schema` entry would be more coupling than the duplication costs. **When a third consumer appears, this becomes a shared package.**

Five other `key === "Enter"` sites are deliberately untouched, because they are activation, not submission — each one also handles Space and sends or commits no field: `apps/desktop/src/views/ToolIoBlock.tsx:69`, `apps/desktop/src/views/WorkspacePanel.tsx:528`, `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/ListSelect.tsx:167`, `apps/web/src/IdeaTreeCanvas.tsx:287`, `apps/web/src/MemoryGraphView.tsx:155`.

### Test support

The desktop app has no DOM test environment, so the three desktop sites are driven through `apps/desktop/tests/support/dom-renderer.ts`, which re-exports `act` and `create` from `react-test-renderer` — the same renderer `apps/web` already uses. That adds a real devDependency to the desktop app rather than reaching into the web app's `node_modules`:

- `apps/desktop/package.json`: `"react-test-renderer": "19.2.7"`. `apps/web/package.json:56` already declares the same version in its own `devDependencies`, so this follows the repository's existing shape — each app declares the test renderer its own tests import — instead of introducing a dependency. The two apps are separate workspace packages, so `apps/desktop` cannot resolve a dependency only `apps/web` declares, and reaching into `apps/web/node_modules` would tie the desktop suite to the web app's install.
- `pnpm-lock.yaml`: three lines in the `apps/desktop` importer's `devDependencies` only (`packages`/`snapshots` unchanged — the version was already resolved for `apps/web`). This was edited by hand, not by `pnpm install`: a plain `pnpm install` on this branch also upgrades `@types/d3-selection`, `@types/d3-zoom` and `@types/ssh2`, which does not belong in this change. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --lockfile-only` exits 0 on the result: the lockfile already agrees with both `package.json` files, so the frozen install CI runs resolves the same tree and never rewrites it. Its only side effect here is dropping the file's UTF-8 BOM, so the commit keeps the BOM.
- `apps/desktop/tests/support/react-test-renderer.d.ts`: the package ships no types and the desktop `tsconfig` includes `tests/**`, so it needs a local declaration.

`App.tsx` is the session shell: mounting it needs a live session client, the router and the async bootstrap that creates the run before the header exists, so a component test would spend its assertions on the mount machinery and would be one fixture away from testing something other than the guard under change. Its test therefore pins the source line, the approach this repository already takes in `apps/web/tests/artifactTree.test.tsx:234`, `:248`, `:300` and `apps/web/tests/ArtifactLifecycleControls.test.tsx:148`. The pin asserts the guard's exact shape, so an edit that drops the rule fails the test instead of regressing silently.

## Validation

Branch shape: `865102a336d9ed972fd073b7eecbcf10ae79ed4c` (upstream `main`) → `760c810d0ae157376cb918c5349a99ef770ae6f9` (tests only, red) → `a876b947b40df1dfd1757b6006db9655d0b93d6b` (fix, this tip).

Base suite on `865102a3`, before this branch:

```
apps/web      # tests 1182  # pass 1182  # fail 0
apps/desktop  # tests 712   # pass 712   # fail 0
```

Red at the tests-only commit `760c810d0ae157376cb918c5349a99ef770ae6f9`, where `apps/web/src/ime-enter.ts` is still a stub, run on that commit before the fix:

```
apps/web      # tests 1199  # pass 1189  # fail 10
apps/desktop  # tests 718   # pass 715   # fail 3
```

The desktop failures are the three user-visible ones: `expected: 1 actual: 2` (a second `/api/remote-hosts/key-files` request), `expected: false actual: true` (the field blurred and committed), `expected: '' actual: 'gpt-4o-mini'` (the model was picked by the Enter that belonged to the IME). The web failures include the key-file browser browsing `+ [ "~/.ssh" ]` where `[]` was expected, the `keyCode: 229` rename that still blurred, and the two `App.tsx` pins. The control cases (composition ended, Shift+Enter left to the caller, non-Enter keys) pass on both sides.

Green at this tip:

```
apps/web      # tests 1199  # pass 1199  # fail 0
apps/desktop  # tests 718   # pass 718   # fail 0
```

The delta against the base is exactly the new tests: 1182 + 17 = 1199 and 712 + 6 = 718.

## Ran

- `cd apps/web && ../../node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` → 1199 tests, 1199 pass, 0 fail.
- `cd apps/desktop && ../../node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` → 718 tests, 718 pass, 0 fail (712 on this branch's base; the new file adds 6).
- `cd apps/web && ../../node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` → exit 0.
- `cd apps/desktop && ../../node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` → exit 0, on the tests-only commit too (the local declaration is enough there).
- `git grep -n 'key === "Enter"\|key !== "Enter"' -- apps/web/src apps/desktop/src` → 7 hits: the two rule bodies and the five activation sites above. No listener keeps its own submission predicate.
- `git grep -n 'nativeEvent.isComposing' -- apps/web/src apps/desktop/src` → no hit; both half-guards now go through the rule.

One note for reproducing the desktop numbers: a working copy whose `apps/desktop/node_modules` predates this devDependency fails the new file with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: react-test-renderer` — that is the install, not the code. After `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (what CI does) the suite is 718 on a fresh clone with no extra linking. Linking the renderer in from a *different* pnpm store produces a duplicate-React `TypeError` instead, so the numbers above were measured with every package resolved from one store.

## Not run

- No browser or IME journey: the files touched have no page test in this repository, and the composition timing belongs to the platform. Acceptance here is the pure rule, the rendered component tests for the three desktop sites, and the existing suites staying green.
- `apps/web/tsconfig.json` and `apps/desktop/tsconfig.json` do not include each app's `tests/` directory, so the two `tsc` runs above do not type-check the new test files, and CI's `pnpm typecheck` (package tsconfigs plus `tsconfig.tests.json`) does not either. A probe that widens the app tsconfigs to `tests/**` fails on `main` already, in files this branch does not touch (`TS2591` for `node:assert`, `TS7016` for `react-test-renderer` in `apps/web/tests/ConfigurationRequestCard.test.tsx`), so this branch does not fix or regress that gap; the desktop side gets a local `react-test-renderer` declaration so its own tests are typed.
- Root `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` still fails with the 7 pre-existing module-resolution errors in `packages/execution-router` and `services/api` reported on `#785` and `#792`; none is in `apps`.

## Labels

If the token cannot apply a `release:*` label, a maintainer needs to add exactly one (the previous PR hit a 403 there).

832.body:
[Bug]: Anthropic Messages UI errors report OpenAI stream and unsupported reasoning_split

Fixes #822

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## Review answers — F1 on `385e48a2`

**F1 (high, must-fix): a Swarm-side constant overrode the run's configured thinking mode.** Fixed on this tip `99491977c7d04bf0ad235e8dbfabad0aa2a130b0`; the run's own choice now decides, and the flag only decides while that choice is open.

The translation now runs through one expression, in the order the review prescribed:

```ts
const thinkingMode = body.thinking ? body.thinking.type as "enabled" | "disabled"
  : endpoint.thinkingMode === undefined || endpoint.thinkingMode === "auto"
    ? (typeof body.reasoning_split === "boolean" ? (body.reasoning_split ? "enabled" : "disabled") : undefined)
    : undefined;
requestEndpoint = { ...endpoint, ...(thinkingMode ? { thinkingMode } : {}) };
```

- `body.thinking` (the request's own control) still wins outright.
- An endpoint that already carries `enabled` or `disabled` — the conversation-level choice the run started with — is left untouched, so `reasoning_split: true` can no longer turn thinking back on behind a user who switched it off.
- Only `auto` (or no mode at all) is the flag's to decide.

On the review's test sentence, which asks that `auto` also stay unchanged: `auto` is not a mode that can be "turned on", and the flag deciding it is the review's own fix expression. Measured through `createModelRequest` (MiniMax-M3, `anthropic-messages`) the three modes serialize as:

| endpoint `thinkingMode` | serialized request |
|---|---|
| `auto` | no thinking field at all — the provider default |
| `enabled` | `thinking: {"type":"adaptive","display":"summarized"}` + `output_config: {"effort":"high"}` |
| `disabled` | `thinking: {"type":"disabled"}` |

So the case that mattered — a run started with thinking **off** silently getting the adaptive control — is now closed, and `auto` is pinned by its own test as flag-decided, which is what the fix expression does.

Tests added by this round:

- `a run's own thinking mode wins over the Swarm reasoning_split flag` — `disabled` with `reasoning_split: true` stays `disabled`, `enabled` with `reasoning_split: false` stays `enabled`.
- `an auto thinking mode lets the Swarm reasoning_split flag decide` — `auto` and `undefined`, both flag values, each resolving to the flag's mode.

## What changed

The model gateway now accepts Swarm's `reasoning_split` and translates it into the endpoint's thinking mode. It is a transport flag, not a provider field, so it never travels further:

- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:274` — `reasoning_split` joins the accepted inbound fields, so it is no longer refused as unknown.
- `:293-297` — the flag becomes the endpoint's `thinkingMode` (`true` → `enabled`, `false` → `disabled`) **only when the run has no explicit mode**; `body.thinking` and an endpoint already set to `enabled`/`disabled` both win over it.
- `:84-85` — the field is declared on `ChatRequest`, so the gateway says what it accepts.

Nothing else moves. `toModelRequest` (`:113-125`) builds `{ history, systemPrompt, tools }` field by field rather than spreading the body, so the flag cannot reach the provider request; the new tests assert both halves (endpoint carries `thinkingMode`, serialized endpoint carries no `reasoning_split`) and that a parameter the gateway genuinely cannot honour (`frequency_penalty`) is still a 400.

### Why the run failed before any provider call

| Evidence | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| `jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:275` throws `Unsupported gateway parameters: …` inside the admission `try`, and `:255` `fail(400, …)` writes `{"error":{"message":…,"type":"model_gateway_error"}}` | the `400` and the `type` in the report are produced by this repository's loopback gateway, not by the provider |
| the upstream-error path (`Model request failed with status …`, `packages/model/src/client.ts:576`) adds a prefix the reported text does not have | the request never left the gateway, so nothing was sent to Anthropic or to MiniMax and then refused |
| `jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:38` — "The model, as JiuwenSwarm sees it: an OpenAI chat-completions endpoint on loopback" | the inbound hop is chat-completions even when the run's endpoint is Anthropic Messages, which is why a chat-completions-only flag can arrive on an Anthropic run at all |

So the report is one failure with two confusing labels: a chat-completions flag arriving on the inbound hop, refused by a whitelist that was written before Swarm started sending it.

### Why `reasoning_split` is there

In this repository the token only exists in `packages/model/src/client.ts:731` (`chatThinkingFields`, `variant === "minimax"`) — an **outbound** field the model client writes for a MiniMax model. The one the gateway refused arrived **inbound** in Swarm's body, which sets the same flag for a MiniMax model. The Anthropic path never writes it (`toAnthropicMessages`/`anthropicThinkingFields` carry no such field), so it should never have been able to fail an Anthropic Messages run.

### What this does not change

The outer wording, `openAI API async stream error: BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {…}`, belongs to JiuwenSwarm's own OpenAI client, an external package; this repository has no such literal (`services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/events.py` only forwards `run.failed`'s reason). This PR makes the run stop failing on the flag. Renaming that outer line is an adapter/upstream change and is out of scope here.

## Validation

Before the first fix, the same request against the gateway returns `400 Unsupported gateway parameters: reasoning_split`; after it, `200`, and the endpoint still resolves to `anthropic-messages` rather than falling back to chat-completions.

Commits, in order: `5caedeaf` (test: accept the flag) → `385e48a2` (fix) → `a3103cac` (test: the run's mode wins) → `99491977` (fix, this tip).

Red at the first tests-only commit `5caedeaf54f05654d817679fc13f1c13d75f5db7`, where the whitelist is still unchanged:

```
services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.test.ts   # tests 53  # pass 52  # fail 1
not ok 53 - a MiniMax reasoning_split transport flag from Swarm is honoured, not rejected as an unknown parameter
```

Red at the second tests-only commit `a3103cac13a66342860c123611848105110f35b9`, where the precedence is still the wrong way round:

```
services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.test.ts   # tests 55  # pass 54  # fail 1
not ok 54 - a run's own thinking mode wins over the Swarm reasoning_split flag
  error: thinkingMode:"disabled" plus reasoning_split:true must keep the run's choice: 'enabled' !== 'disabled'
```

Green at this tip `99491977c7d04bf0ad235e8dbfabad0aa2a130b0`:

```
services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.test.ts   # tests 55  # pass 55  # fail 0
```

## Ran

- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.test.ts`: 55 tests, 55 pass, 0 fail at this tip; 54 pass, 1 fail at the precedence red commit; 52 pass, 1 fail at the first tests-only commit.
- `typecheck`: exit 0.
- A local probe of the reported shape: an Anthropic endpoint plus `reasoning_split: true` went from `400 Unsupported gateway parameters` to `200`, with the endpoint still `anthropic-messages`.
- The precedence probe: `{ thinkingMode: "disabled" }` plus `reasoning_split: true` now keeps `disabled` and serializes `thinking: {"type":"disabled"}`; before the fix the same input produced `enabled` and the adaptive control.
- `git grep -n 'reasoning_split' -- services packages apps` → the field is accepted and translated in the gateway, written for MiniMax only in `packages/model/src/client.ts:731`, and nowhere serialized to a provider.

## Not run

- No live call to a real Anthropic or MiniMax endpoint: the gateway is exercised against the repository's fake streamer, which is what pins the failure (the request never left the gateway in the first place).
- No UI journey: the user-visible change is that the run no longer fails with this 400 and no longer overrides the run's thinking mode; the surface that renders the error is unchanged.

## Labels

If the token cannot apply a `release:*` label, a maintainer needs to add exactly one (the previous PR hit a 403 there).

832.title: fix(api): honour Swarm's MiniMax reasoning_split as a thinking flag instead of failing the run

833.author: HugoXK
833.body: Fixes #828 ## Review answers — the three threads on `c4292825` All three are fixed on this tip `a3b1e688160d40caa9c37dbedc5fe4971497a355`, one red-first commit pair each, on the same branch and the same base `865102a3` (no rebase). **F1 — `inferCsv.ts:225` (high, must-fix): padding every row to the widest record is O(rows × max width).** Reproduced here before touching it. Fixture: 3-column header, 20,000 ordinary rows, one record with 500 cells — before **12.7 s / 1050 MB heap / 500 columns / 10,020,501 cells**, after **264 ms / 30 MB / 6 columns / 140,007 cells**. (The review measured 5.5 s / 1.2 GB on its own fixture: same cause, same order.) The bound is **surplus columns = `min(16, max(2, header width))`**, so a table materialises at most `2 × header width` cells per row (`3 ×` for a one-column header). **Header columns are not part of the bound** — a legitimate 200-column header still returns 200 columns, one cell per row. Past the bound the trailing surplus cells are joined into the last surplus column, and `table.warnings` gains one entry (`csv.importSurplusColumns`, en and zhCN). Tests: `caps surplus columns so one wide record cannot widen every row` (6 columns, `cells <= rows × 7`, warning `497 cells past the header`) and `keeps a legitimate wide header without folding its columns` (200 columns, `width + 1` keys per row). **F2 — `inferCsv.ts:224` (medium): a real `__parsed_extra` column lost its own value.** Fixed, but not with the array check as suggested, because that check cannot separate the two shapes. papaparse 5.5.4 (`papaparse.js:1303–1311`) routes on the **field name**, not on overflow: `if (field === '__parsed_extra') { row[field] = row[field] || []; row[field].push(value); }`. A header column literally named `__parsed_extra` therefore also arrives as an array — measured on this branch: `a,__parsed_extra\n1,x\n` → `fields ["a","__parsed_extra"]`, `data [{"a":"1","__parsed_extra":["x"]}]`. So the discriminator is the header: when it contains that name, the first array element is that column's value and only the remaining ones are surplus; the key is deleted only in the branch where the header does not claim it. Tests pin both shapes — `a,__parsed_extra\n1,x\n` keeps columns `a,__parsed_extra` with `x` in place, `a,__parsed_extra\n1,x,9\n` yields `a,__parsed_extra,__extra_1` with `x` and `9`. **F3 — `inferCsv.ts:110` (medium): column order still came from `Object.keys`.** Fixed as suggested: `rectangularizeRows` returns the ordered id list (header in file order, then surplus) and `profileRows` takes it as an optional argument, keeping the key union as the fallback for callers that only have rows. Tests: `10,2` → columns `['10','2']`, grid header `["#","10","2"]`, export header `10,2`; `2024,2025,2` stays `['2024','2025','2']`. This one is pre-existing, and it is folded into this PR because the ordering it breaks is exactly this PR's stated goal — that is the scope note, stated rather than implied. ## What changed Six files, and the split matters for review: | file | change | what it is | |---|---|---| | `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/csv/inferCsv.ts` | +99/−6 | the fix and the surplus bound | | `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/chart-spec/filters.ts` | +25/−4 | positional export helper, old helper deleted | | `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/components/VirtualDataTable.tsx` | +2/−1 | header cell renders the name, not the id | | `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/CsvArtifactWindow.tsx` | +2/−2 | export calls the positional helper | | `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` | +2/−0 | the surplus-fold warning, en and zhCN | | `apps/web/tests/CsvArtifact.test.tsx` | +174/−3 | tests only | `parseCsvText` decided a table's columns from the union of the parsed rows' keys (everything except `__rowId`), while `:222` read the real header `result.meta.fields` only to pass it to `inferTableKind`. Line numbers in this section are `865102a3`'s, i.e. before the change. Two symptoms followed, and they are the same bug seen from both sides: - a row wider than the header made Papa Parse park the surplus cells on the record under its internal key `__parsed_extra`, which then became a sortable, typed, exported column named after a library internal — one surplus cell as a bare number, two or more joined by commas (`"3,4"`); - a header column that no row filled had no key in the union, so it was absent from `columns` altogether — not empty, not hidden: invisible to the viewer, the chart field list and the CSV export. The table is now built from the header, losslessly: - Width is the header's own columns plus the bounded surplus columns (F1 above); the header's names stay first and in the file's order, taken from `meta.fields`. - Every record is rebuilt to that width: `__parsed_extra` is removed (except where the header claims the name, F2), missing header cells are set to `undefined` (profiled as `null`), and surplus values are written back by position, so the key can never become a column id. - Surplus columns get synthetic ids `__extra_1`, `__extra_2`, … with `label: ""` — the same "a column with no name" shape an empty header cell (`a,,c`) already produces today, and the viewer already renders such a column correctly. - `profileRows` takes an optional ordered column list, so a surplus column filled by only some rows cannot come and go and a header column no row fills is still present. Two supporting changes follow from that: - **The header cell must render the name, not the id.** `VirtualDataTable.tsx:96` printed `column.id`, which is what made `__parsed_extra` — and two spaces, from `label: " parsed extra"` — visible to a reader. It now renders `columnHeaderName(column)` (`label === "" ? "" : column.id`), a shared predicate also used by the export so the grid and the exported header cannot drift apart. `:95`'s sort `title` still carries the id: the cell is empty, but the sort control needs an accessible name. - **The export has to be positional.** It called `rowsToCsv(rows, table.columns.map((column) => column.id))`, and that helper uses each field as *both* the value key and the header name. Handing it the header text would have read `row[""]` — the surplus value silently disappearing from the export — and two unnamed columns would have collapsed onto the same object key. `tableToCsv(rows, columns)` builds the header row from the header text and the body cell-by-cell from `column.id`; `rowsToCsv` then had no production caller and is deleted, with its spreadsheet-formula test moved to the new helper. `#654`'s BOM handling of real header names is untouched (checked by probe: `"\uFEFFa,b\r\n1,2\r\n"` → columns `["a","b"]`, row `[1,2]`), and the `rowId` de-duplication below `:108` is untouched (a test pins `__rowId === "row-2"`). One visible behaviour change to call out: in the positional shape a header name is a data value, so it goes through the same formula neutralisation as the cells. A legitimate header starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` therefore gets the `'` prefix — `-log2FC,b` exports as `'-log2FC,b`. This is deliberate: Excel reads `-log2FC` as a formula, and the prefix is the standard text marker that spreadsheet apps do not display. Splitting the rule per column kind would put a header and its own cells under two different policies. Known boundary, pre-existing and left alone: a synthetic id that collides with a real header name is suffixed (`__extra_1_`) to stay unique. ## Ran Branch parent `865102a3`; the suite is **1182 tests** there, measured on that base rather than carried over (it was 1181 on the earlier base this branch started from). Commits, in order: `a1dd498e` (test: overflow cells, their empty header, the export name) → `c8377594` (fix) → `b5521c8e` (test: a formula in the exported header) → `c4292825` (fix) → `98579012` (test: surplus bound) → `1d02ef47` (fix) → `22ca0d3c` (test: real `__parsed_extra` column) → `55c9181c` (fix) → `4ee6fb69` (test: numeric header order) → `a3b1e688` (fix, this tip). - Red at `a1dd498e`, the first test commit, run before `c8377594` landed: **1186 tests / 1182 pass / 4 fail** — 1182 plus the four cases that commit adds, all four red: ``` not ok 203 - keeps overflow cells in unique unnamed columns instead of Papa's internal key error: 'internal key became a column id: __parsed_extra' not ok 204 - pads short rows to the header width so no header column disappears expected: ['a','b','c'] actual: ['a','b'] not ok 205 - the data table header hides an unnamed overflow column's internal id expected: ['#','a','b',''] actual: ['#','a','b','__parsed_extra'] not ok 206 - exports an unnamed overflow column with an empty header name expected: 'a,b,' actual: 'a,b,__parsed_extra' ``` - Red at `b5521c8e`, the second test commit, run before its own fix: ``` 1187 tests / 1186 pass / 1 fail not ok 207 - neutralizes a spreadsheet formula in an exported header name error: |- =SUM(1),b 1,2 code: 'ERR_ASSERTION' expected: true, actual: false, operator: '==' ``` The exported header row is still `=SUM(1),b`. The four cases added by `a1dd498e` are already green in this run, because `c8377594` had landed before it. - The three review fixes, each measured on the file it touches (`apps/web/tests/CsvArtifact.test.tsx`) at the red commit and its own fix: ``` 98579012 (red) 39 tests / 38 pass / 1 fail not ok 9 - caps surplus columns so one wide record cannot widen every row error: 500 !== 6 (every one of the 20,001 rows was laid out 500 wide) 1d02ef47 (fix) 39 / 39 / 0 22ca0d3c (red) 40 / 39 / 1 - keeps a real __parsed_extra column instead of reading it as overflow actual columns: ['a','__parsed_extra','__extra_1'] 55c9181c (fix) 40 / 40 / 0 4ee6fb69 (red) 41 / 40 / 1 - keeps numeric header names in file order actual columns: ['2','10'] a3b1e688 (fix) 41 / 41 / 0 ``` - Green at this tip `a3b1e688160d40caa9c37dbedc5fe4971497a355`, whole web suite: **1191 / 1191 / 0** — 1182 plus the nine cases this branch adds. - `tsc -p apps/web/tsconfig.json --noEmit` → exit 0. `apps/web`'s tsconfig includes only `src/**`, so the test file was type-checked separately with the same compiler options minus that `include` → exit 0. - `tsc -p apps/desktop/tsconfig.json --noEmit` → exit 0. No desktop source is touched; the run is there to show the branch moves nothing else. - `#650`'s quoted-newline case still runs and passes (`ok 214 - counts quoted newlines as part of one data record…`). What the earlier cases assert, by value rather than by shape: - `a,b\n1,2,3\n` → columns `a,b,__extra_1` with labels `["a","b",""]`, the value `3` under `__extra_1`; `a,b\n1,2,3,4\n` → `3` and `4` under `__extra_1`/`__extra_2`; no `id` or `label` anywhere equals `__parsed_extra`, every row's key order equals the column order, and `__rowId` is still `row-2`. - mixed widths `a,b\n1,2,3\n7,8\n` → `[[1,2,3],[7,8,null]]`. - `a,b,c\n1,2\n` → `c` kept as a column with `null` and `missingCount 1`. - rendering the real `VirtualDataTable`: header span texts `["#","a","b",""]`, no `__extra_1` in the document, and `title="Sort by __extra_1"` still present. - `tableToCsv` first line `a,b,` (`a,b,,` for two unnamed columns) with body `1,2,3` / `1,2,3,4` intact, and the migrated formula test asserting `'=SUM(1)` in the header row while a plain `a,b` header is unchanged. - `rowsToCsv` has no remaining reference in `apps/`, `services/` or `packages/`. ## Not run - No browser journey: the change is the CSV parse, render and export path, and the assertions above drive the real `VirtualDataTable` and the real export helper rather than a mock. - No manifest, lockfile or dependency change; `apps/desktop` has no source change. ## Labels If the token cannot apply a `release:*` label, a maintainer needs to add exactly one (the previous PR hit a 403 there).
833.head: dev1/fix/csv-parsed-extra-column
833.title: fix(web): build a CSV table from the header, not from the parsed rows' keys

834.author: qingkwl
834.body:
## 概述

Windows 桌面端安装包体积优化：f26 基线 **797.6 MiB → 578.0 MiB（−27.5%，实测）**，同时完成 6 个 Python env → 2 个的合并。中文设计/决策记录见 #807，English version: #808。

硬约束全程保持：**离线双击即用、首启零网络、首启不变慢**（W15 全量 pyc 预编译不触碰，且 assemble 现对预编译失败硬失败）。

## 波次（每波独立出包验证）

| 波 | 内容 | 安装包 |
|---|---|---|
| W1 | JW 死重清除（extras 收口 238MB / lint 组 / k8s·onnx·babel·adk 传递依赖清扫 codex vendor 剔除）+ JW patch 0018（playwright/uv 移出主依赖） | 613.4 MiB |
| W2 | 5 服务 venv → uv workspace 单 venv（统一 lock 68 包就高：fastapi 0.162/websockets 17.4/pydantic 2.14） | 583.3 MiB |
| W3 | JW patch 0019 版本对齐（numpy 2.5.4/pandas 3.1.0；websockets cap<18，17 被 google-genai 钉死故维持 15.0.1）；硬链接去重经实测证伪后关闭（7z 窗口机制+venv 隔离，见 issue 正文） | — |
| W4 | assemble 四道门禁（JW 预编译硬失败/载荷 import 自证/RequiredFiles 清单/尺寸常显）+ Electron locales 55→3 pak | **578.0 MiB** |

补丁链 manifest：13 → **16**（0018-desktop-slim-deps / 0019-align-workspace-versions，均含 uv.lock 重生成 + hunk 纯度核对）。

## 质量证据

- 壳单测 118/118（新增 payload-slim 规则库单测）；服务测试与 f26 基线树逐一对照零回归（evolve 33 个失败为 Windows 无沙箱既有问题）
- 每波全链冒烟：adapter /agent/info reachable；assemble 四查全绿（预编译 4/4、自证 import 2/2、清单 9/9）
- 载荷抽查：审计死重 7/7 不在、活包全保留、JW pyc 29087 全量
- 成品：签名✅ blockmap✅ locales=en-US/zh-CN/zh-TW✅

## 回退

每波可独立 revert（三个独立 commit）；补丁链 0018/0019 可 apply --reverse。

## 待办（非本 PR 阻塞）

- 真机 GUI 安装三档验证（进行中，结果将回填 #807/#808）
- 剩余可选杠杆待拍板：evolve candidates extra（−~25 MiB）、飞书 lark_oapi、imageio_ffmpeg/matplotlib 审计
834.head: sizeopt/f26-6to2
834.title: feat(sizeopt): Windows installer 797.6 → 578.0 MiB (−27.5%), 6→2 env merge + payload slimming
